subject: physics_2
question_text: Under what conditions will a wave be reflected?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. Physics hand-checked: reflection happens at any boundary where the wave impedance changes — fully where the medium ends abruptly (a rigid wall), and partially wherever the density or the elastic properties (rigidity) of the medium change, with the rest of the wave transmitted.

recall_prompt: Say the two conditions under which a wave is reflected.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Medium ends abruptly
lines: A progressive wave is reflected when the
medium ends abruptly at any point — for
steps.margin_note: First mark. The full-reflection case: the medium simply stops.
steps.why: Where the medium stops, the wave energy cannot continue forward, so the wave must come back — this is the complete-reflection case.
common_mistakes: Saying a wave reflects only from a rigid wall — a free end also reflects; the condition is the medium ending, rigid or free.

recall.must_convey: That a wave reflects where the medium ends abruptly, such as at a rigid boundary.
accept: the wave cannot continue so it comes back

steps.memory_tip: No medium ahead — the wave has to come back.

steps.label: Change of density or rigidity
steps.mark_note: Partial reflection at a property change
lines: A wave is partially reflected wherever
property) of the medium changes; the
rest of the wave is transmitted.

lines.text: A wave reflects where the medium changes

steps.margin_note: Second mark. The partial case — name BOTH properties, density and rigidity.
steps.why: The wave speed is set by the medium's density and elasticity. Where either changes, the speed changes, and part of the wave cannot cross the join — that part returns as the reflected wave.
common_mistakes: Naming only density — the elastic property (rigidity) is the other half of the condition.
Calling this complete reflection — at a property change the wave splits: part reflected, part transmitted.

recall.must_convey: That a wave is partially reflected wherever the density or rigidity of the medium changes.
accept: partial reflection at a change of density
change of rigidity reflects part of the wave

steps.memory_tip: Full stop → full reflection. Property change → partial reflection.

insider_note: Two conditions, two marks: the medium ending (full reflection) and the medium changing (partial). Naming both density and rigidity in the second protects it.
